fact.title: Did you know?
fact.pig: A pig loves to roll in the mud. That keeps it nice and cool!
fact.cow: A cow eats grass all day long. We make cheese from her milk!
fact.sheep: The sheep wears a thick coat of wool. We make warm jumpers from that wool.
fact.horse: Did you know a horse can sleep standing up? It does not fall over!
fact.donkey: Can you hear that? The donkey calls hee-haw! With its long ears it hears everything.
fact.goat: A goat climbs on everything. Even on high rocks!
fact.alpaca: The alpaca has very soft wool. When it is happy, it hums softly.
fact.chicken: Cluck cluck cluck! A hen lays an egg almost every day.
fact.duck: A duck's feathers do not get wet. The water just rolls off!
fact.rabbit: When a rabbit is happy, it jumps high in the air!
fact.zebra: Every zebra has different stripes. No two are the same!
fact.giraffe: Nobody is as tall as the giraffe! It can reach the leaves at the very top of the tree.
fact.lion: A lion sleeps almost all day. Just like a big, lazy cat!
fact.camel: There is fat in a camel's hump. That is how it can go a long time without food.
fact.rhino: The rhino loves a mud bath. That way its skin does not burn in the sun.
fact.hippo: The hippo lies in the water all day. Only its eyes and ears stick out.
fact.elephant: With its trunk an elephant can smell, drink and take a shower!
fact.ostrich: The ostrich cannot fly, but it can run very fast. And it lays the biggest egg in the world!
fact.cheetah: The cheetah is the fastest animal on land. Whoosh, off it goes!
fact.gazelle: Boing! A gazelle jumps high in the air with all four legs at once.
fact.monkey: A monkey swings from branch to branch. It can hold things with its hands and with its feet!
fact.parrot: A parrot can learn words. It just says what you say!
fact.tiger: Many cats do not like water. But the tiger loves to swim!
fact.gorilla: Every evening a gorilla makes a new bed of leaves.
fact.crocodile: Mother crocodile carries her babies to the water very gently in her mouth.
fact.panda: The panda eats bamboo almost all day long. It sits down to eat, just like you!
fact.peacock: Look, the peacock opens its tail! It looks like a big fan full of eyes.
fact.toucan: The toucan has a very big beak. But that beak is very light!
fact.sloth: The sloth does everything very slowly. It likes to hang upside down from a branch.
fact.panther: The panther is very good at climbing trees. It likes to rest up there.
fact.penguin: A penguin cannot fly. But under water it swims so fast that it looks like flying!
fact.seal: A seal uses its whiskers to feel where the fish are swimming.
fact.polarbear: The polar bear's fur is white. But the skin underneath is black!
fact.reindeer: With reindeer, both the daddies and the mummies have antlers on their heads.
fact.wolf: Wolves howl together: awoo! That is how they tell each other: here I am!
fact.arcticfox: The arctic fox is white in winter and brown in summer. That makes it very hard to spot!
fact.bear: All winter long the bear sleeps in its den. In spring it wakes up again.
fact.yak: The yak has a very long, thick coat. So it never gets cold in the mountains.
fact.owl: Shh! An owl flies without a sound. And it can turn its head almost all the way round.
fact.walrus: The walrus has two long tusks. It uses them to pull itself out of the water onto the ice.
fact.flamingo: Why is the flamingo pink? That comes from its food! And it sleeps on one leg.
fact.turtle: The tortoise always carries its house on its back. So it is at home everywhere!
fact.otter: Otters hold hands when they sleep. That way they do not float away!
fact.beaver: The beaver gnaws down trees with its strong teeth. It builds a house in the water from the branches.
fact.pelican: The pelican has a pouch under its beak. It scoops up fish with it, just like a fishing net!
fact.koala: The koala sleeps in a tree almost all day. And it only eats leaves.
fact.redpanda: The red panda uses its fluffy tail as a blanket. Nice and warm!
fact.lemur: Lemurs love to sit in the morning sun. Tummy forward, arms out wide!
fact.bison: The bison loves to roll in the sand. That is how it scratches its back when it itches!
fact.kangaroo: A baby kangaroo lives in the pouch on its mummy's tummy. It is warm and safe in there.
fact.dolphin: Dolphins talk to each other with whistles and clicks. Every dolphin has its own whistle, just like a name!
fact.orca: The orca is really a very big dolphin. It always swims together with its family.
fact.ray: The ray is as flat as a pancake. It swims as if it is flying under water!
fact.shark: A shark keeps getting new teeth. When one falls out, a new one grows right back!

say.level.21: The gazelle jumps around. Watch out: animals can get sick!
say.level.22: Welcome to the jungle! The monkey climbs. Build a high net!
say.level.23: The parrot can fly. It wants a high net too.
say.level.24: The tiger is strong and sleeps in a den.
say.level.25: The gorilla is very strong and eats leaves.
say.level.26: The crocodile wants water and a stone wall.
say.level.28: The peacock shows its beautiful feathers.
say.level.29: The toucan has a big beak and likes fruit.
say.level.30: The sloth is very slow. It likes to hang in a climbing tree.
say.level.31: The panther sneaks around. Watch out: an animal might escape!
say.level.32: Welcome to the ice! The penguin wants snow and fish.
say.level.33: The seal loves to swim. Give it water and fish.
say.level.34: The polar bear is strong. Build a stone wall in the snow!

say.level.37: The arctic fox is as white as snow.
say.level.38: The brown bear lives in the forest and eats fish.
say.level.39: The yak has a thick, warm coat.
say.level.40: The snowy owl can fly. Build a high net!
say.level.41: The walrus has long tusks. And now to faraway lands!
say.level.42: The flamingo is pink and likes to stand in the water.
say.level.43: The tortoise is slow and wants sand.
say.level.44: The otter swims and eats fish.
say.level.45: The beaver builds a lodge. It wants water.
say.level.46: The pelican catches fish with its big beak.
say.level.47: The koala sleeps in a climbing tree and eats leaves.
say.level.48: The red panda eats bamboo and loves to climb.
say.level.49: The lemur has a long tail with stripes.
say.level.50: The bison is big and strong. This is the last level!

say.event.new: Look, a card! A guest is asking for help. Tap it for a little puzzle, or tap the cross if you do not feel like it.
say.event.class.sum.1: Hello! Our whole class is here. Can you help me with a sum?
say.event.class.sum.2: Hi there! The children love doing sums. Will you help us?
say.event.class.count.1: Are all the children still here? Can you help me count them?
say.event.class.count.2: Oh dear, I have lost count! Will you help me count the children?
say.event.class.draw.1: The children are drawing an animal. Can you help me with its name?
say.event.class.draw.2: We are making a lovely drawing. Which letters go with it? Will you help?
say.event.class.line.1: The children are lining up. Will you help, from small to big?
say.event.class.line.2: Everything has to be in a neat row. Can you help me with the order?
say.event.class.guide.1: Hello! We are looking for an animal. Can you show me the way?
say.event.class.guide.2: Hi there! The children want to see an animal. Will you help us find it?
say.event.class.go.1: This is the animal we are looking for. Tap the place where it lives!
say.event.class.good.1: Well done! Thank you. The children are cheering for you.
say.event.class.good.2: How clever of you! Now the class can carry on. Thank you!
say.event.class.good.3: Hooray, that is exactly right! You are a great helper.
say.event.class.bad.1: What a pity, that was not right. Never mind, better luck next time!
say.event.class.bad.2: Oh, that was tricky. It does not matter, we will try again later.
say.event.class.guide.good.1: Thank you! We will walk there now. The children are happy.
say.event.class.guide.good.2: Well done, that is its home! Come along, children, let us go and look.
say.event.class.bye.good.1: We are going back to school. What a lovely park, we will come back!
say.event.class.bye.good.2: Goodbye! The children loved it. See you next time!
say.event.class.bye.good.3: It was a lovely day. Thank you, we would love to come again!
say.event.class.bye.bad.1: We are going home. There was not much to see yet. What a pity!
say.event.class.bye.bad.2: Goodbye! The children wanted to see more animals. Maybe next time.
say.event.party.1: It is someone's birthday! Will you help put the presents in a row?
say.event.party.2: Hooray, a party! Can you help? Put the presents from small to big.
say.event.party.good.1: Hooray! The birthday child loves the presents.
say.event.party.good.2: Lovely! Now the party can begin. Thank you!
say.event.party.bad.1: Oops, that went wrong. Luckily there is still cake!
say.event.party.bad.2: What a pity, the presents are all mixed up. The party goes on anyway!
say.event.celeb.1: There is a famous guest in the park! Will you help him with a word?
say.event.celeb.2: Look, a famous guest! He is looking for the right letters. Will you help?
say.event.celeb.good.1: The famous guest thinks you are very clever!
say.event.celeb.good.2: The famous guest claps for you. Well done!
say.event.celeb.bad.1: The famous guest shrugs. What a pity!
say.event.celeb.bad.2: The word did not work out. The famous guest walks on.
say.event.delivery.1: A truck full of food is at the gate! Will you help count?
say.event.delivery.2: Toot toot! The truck is here. Will you help count the crates of food?
say.event.delivery.good.1: It all adds up! The driver gives you coins.
say.event.delivery.good.2: Well counted! All the food is here. Here are some coins for you.
say.event.delivery.bad.1: Oops, counted wrong. The truck drives away again.
say.event.delivery.bad.2: The counting went wrong. Never mind, another truck will come tomorrow.
say.event.photo.1: A photographer from the newspaper is here! Will you help with the word under the photo?
say.event.photo.2: Click! A photo for the newspaper. Will you help with the letters?
say.event.photo.good.1: The park will be in the newspaper! More guests are coming now.
say.event.photo.good.2: What a lovely photo! Everyone will read about our park in the newspaper.
say.event.photo.bad.1: The photographer does not know the word. No photo in the newspaper.
say.event.photo.bad.2: What a pity, the word is not right. The photographer will come back another time.
say.event.build.1: I am busy building. Can you help me? Put everything in order.
say.event.build.2: My things are all mixed up! Will you help, from small to big?
say.event.build.good.1: Thank you! Now I can carry on building. Here are a few coins.
say.event.build.good.2: What a good helper you are! Everything is neat again.
say.event.build.bad.1: Oops, that does not fit yet. Never mind, I will measure it again myself.
say.event.build.bad.2: That did not go well yet. Next time we will build together again!
say.event.bedtime.1: It is getting dark. I am counting the animals. Can you help me count?
say.event.bedtime.2: Are all the animals still here? Will you help me count before bedtime?
say.event.bedtime.good.1: All the animals are here! Now they can sleep well. Thank you.
say.event.bedtime.good.2: Well counted! Good night, dear animals. You were a lovely help.
say.event.bedtime.bad.1: Oh dear, I have lost count. Never mind, I will count again later.
say.event.bedtime.bad.2: That was not quite right. Never mind, the animals will sleep well anyway.
say.event.crates.1: There are new crates of food. Can you help me put them in order?
say.event.crates.2: So many crates! Will you help? Put them from small to big.
say.event.crates.good.1: All in a neat row! Now I can find the food easily. Thank you!
say.event.crates.good.2: Well done! The animals will get a lovely meal soon.
say.event.crates.bad.1: Oops, the crates are all mixed up. I will tidy them up myself.
say.event.crates.bad.2: That did not work yet. Never mind, next time it will go well!
say.event.till.1: I am counting the coins in the till. Can you help me count?
say.event.till.2: So many coins today! Will you help? Then we can count them together.
say.event.till.good.1: That is exactly right! Here, a few coins for you.
say.event.till.good.2: Well counted! The till is right. Thank you for helping.
say.event.till.bad.1: Oops, the count is not right. I will count the coins once more.
say.event.till.bad.2: What a pity, that was not right. Never mind, counting is quite hard!
say.event.mayor.1: The mayor is visiting! He wants to know an animal's name. Will you help?
say.event.mayor.2: The mayor is asking about the animals. Can you help me with the word?
say.event.mayor.good.1: The mayor is proud of our park! He is telling everyone about it.
say.event.mayor.good.2: How clever! The mayor is inviting even more guests.
say.event.mayor.bad.1: The mayor does not understand the word. What a pity, he is going home.
say.event.mayor.bad.2: That did not work. Never mind, the mayor had a nice time anyway.
